# Metric reconciliation

*Generated by `src/metric_reconciliation.py` on 2026-10-17. Proposed by Marwa (Claude Code teammate 2) for the ANALYSIS.md team action "agree one definition for each number that differs between documents". **Status: agreed by Omar and Marwa, 2026-10-17.** Values use raw lines (AGENTS.md); the deduplicated value is shown where it differs.*

| Metric | Proposed definition and wording | Value (raw lines) | Value (repeats dropped) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| **Single-item orders** | Share of orders that contain only one distinct product (any quantity). This is the audience for a different-product add-on. Report as '54% of orders contain only one product'. The one-line (53.6%) and one-unit (50.6%) figures answer different questions; do not use them as the headline. | 53.9% | 53.9% |
| **Retention** | Month-to-month repeat rate of identified customers: of those who ordered in a month, the share who order again the next month (66% on average). Call the 91% figure 'overlap between Jan-Feb and May-Jun customers', never 'retention'. 'New' customers are first OBSERVED, not first ever (README). | 65.6% | 65.6% |
| **Promotion profit effect** | Harbour promo-category gross profit per day during the 16 promo days vs the other days of March and May, minus the same change at Garden and Uptown: -15%. Report it together with the units version and the $471 discount given away, and say it is 16 days, two categories and one branch, so it is not an elasticity. | -14.6% | -14.4% |
| **Tuesday effect** | Orders per Tuesday divided by the average orders per day on Monday and Wednesday-Friday: 1.53x ('Tuesday is about 53% busier than a normal weekday'). Comparing with weekdays keeps the weekend dip out of the Tuesday effect. ANALYSIS.md's 1.66x is also correct but compares with all six other days, including the quiet weekend; if it is used, say 'than the average of the other six days'. Use per-day rates: the period has 25 Wednesdays and 26 of every other weekday. | 1.53x | 1.53x |
| **Standing 10% discount** | Always say lines: '5.6% of product lines get 10% off'. The order-level figure (8.3% of orders contain a 10% line) is a different unit; give it only with the word 'orders'. Notebook 01's 'about 6% of orders' does not match its own table (0.08). | 5.6% | 5.6% |
| **Order growth** | Orders per day, January vs June: +57%. Monthly totals (+52%) understate it slightly because January has 31 days and June 30. | +57.0% | +57.0% |

## Edits needed once agreed

- **ANALYSIS.md (Omar):** item 7 says 'Tuesdays at about 1.66 times other days'. That is correct for 'all six other days'; either keep it and add that wording, or switch to the proposed weekday comparison (1.53x). Item 6 says 'about half of orders contain a single product'; that matches the proposed definition, so add the exact value.
- **Promotion:** no document should quote the pitch's -23% promo profit figure alone. It compares with the 2 weeks before and has no control branches. The proposed difference-in-differences is the headline, with units, gross profit and the discount cost reported together.
- **Notebooks 01-08:** stay as the team's original work (AGENTS.md); the corrections live here and in the README.
- **README (shared):** the figures in the 'Why the numbers move' section already use per-day rates; the old pitch figures (51% single-item, 91% 'retained', -23% promo profit) are superseded by this table.
